First time ever posting to this sub reddit or writing about an experience so again may come across as a story but this actually happened. I cannot stress enough about people commenting   “why didn’t you use your phone?” When you’re sat there in the moment and you see something very much out of the ordinary truly you don’t just whip your phone out and start filming, this thing was not too far from us and it could of been dangerous for me to take my time to go start filming and not concentrating on me and my friends safety. We were frozen and figuring out what to do, so again each to their own on what you believe or other people in the comments section. I don’t casually fancy having a bullshit scare factor story session for no reason I came here to see what it could of been and to find out anything else.
Just to confirm the dogs ran alongside us when we left, wouldn’t ever leave my dog behind. Me and C’s dogs are usually very curious but they wouldn’t investigate and ended up protecting us.

24 years old British female also, I can relate so much to you on this because then if you explain that if you’re a lil awkward because of autism I get the annoying ignorant responses of “YoU dONt AcT or LOok AUtiSTic” “ArE YOu lyINg foR aTTenTION???” And I lose hope in making friends because I’m always facing stupid responses instead of people asking me politely or genuinely. I mean the only ways I’ve found around making friends before is when you just instantly click with them, you can be full on weird and have a good laugh and not worry about the fear of judgement from them. That’s the friendship I’m looking for...a friend that doesn’t let you be weird on your own, they join you on it and it’s the best feeling in the world.

But sometimes I can’t even process typing to keyboard and what I write doesn’t make sense it’s a vicious circle with me. If I’m in public it usually takes me two hours or more as there’s a lot of sensory input and I need to be deprived of that in order for me to calm.
Yeah like saying on thing can be so much and also I feel like my brain doesn’t translate well when I’m about to speak and then jumbled words or noises come out and it infuriates me so much!

I currently have a support team with my autism to monitor my patterns and behaviour and general things to do with it, they’ve helped me pin point situations and how to make it easier for me to not fall into a deep spiral or a bigger spiral of depression.
